summary: You present a clear, well-motivated reef-monitoring mission with a justified single-satellite concept and structured coverage of launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL, supported by STK screenshots. Credibility is reduced by the incorrect SSO inclination (87.79° vs ~97.8°), wrong Kourou latitude, overstated contact duration, missing link/swath calculations and STK files, and weak referencing. Addressing these will lift the report from Adequate toward Accomplished.
next_steps: Correct the orbital geometry: recompute the 600 km SSO inclination (~97.8° retrograde), fix Kourou's latitude (~5.2°N), and re-run STK so text, table and figure agree. Add a GSD/swath calculation to justify the 600 km altitude and clarify why low resolution is undesirable.

Strengthen quantitative evidence: reconcile the mean contact duration (~9.7 min, not almost 20 min), add a link budget/data-rate and ground-station capability analysis, and support the drag-sail EOL with deorbit-lifetime/ballistic-coefficient and debris-mitigation compliance calculations.

Improve evidence and referencing: include STK/PIGI files in an appendix, number and caption all figures/tables, replace the Wikipedia source, ensure citations [49]–[74] appear in the reference list, and explicitly define the operator and customers in the Introduction.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the mission need and single-satellite rationale with references. To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify the operator and customers (not just implicit Australian facilities, UTAS and scientists), add detailed user/operations discussion, and use quality literature rather than bare URLs. Keep the strong rationale.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL with STK screenshots. Next level requires correcting the SSO inclination (~97.8°, not 87.79°), Kourou latitude (~5.2°N) and contact duration (~9.7 min mean); adding GSD/swath and link-budget calculations; including STK files; and supporting drag-sail EOL with deorbit-lifetime and compliance evidence.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion restates launch, orbit and ground-station choices. To reach Accomplished, include key quantitative outcomes (altitude, inclination, contact statistics, mission lifetime), state the EOL approach, and avoid overclaiming a fully described configuration. Tie conclusions directly to evidence in the main body.
criteria.C4: Structure, headings and executive summary are clear. Next level requires numbered/captioned figures and tables, consistent formatting, and a reference list matching all in-text citations (including [49]–[74]); replace Wikipedia with credible sources and proofread grammar. This will make the report professional and easy to follow.
